identity.question: Will Donald Trump win the 2024 US Presidential Election?
identity.rulesSummary: YES if Donald J. Trump wins the 2024 US presidential election. AP, Fox News and NBC must all call the same winner; if they had not agreed by January 20, 2025, the inauguration determined resolution. Neither national popular vote nor winning Iowa defines this contract.

audienceRationale: A criminal verdict, an assassination attempt, an endorsement, a televised debate and a surprise poll are unusually recognizable and distinct campaign moments. The subject needs almost no introduction.
playRationale: A major endorsement sounds helpful, but the retained contract’s stabilized response is negative. The debate and the Iowa poll fall into the same tie group. Players can distinguish the importance of a news story from how much probability was left to move.
tension: The rally shooting measures +10.00 pp; Kennedy’s endorsement −1.175, conviction −2.00, debate −2.575 and Iowa poll −3.45. The frozen set produces three tie groups, not five clean ranks. This remains compelling but repeats the Trump shooting already present in Biden #001, so put two non-election editions first.

selectionFreeze.disclosure: Freeze these five fact clusters per candidate for historical significance before running fresh event-window calculations. Timestamp anchors must come from public evidence, never optimized on prices. Failed candidates stay failed; do not replace weak cards after seeing movements. Raw histories and broad daily-median suitability statistics were examined before this freeze; no new five-card event-window calculations have run. Prior project records contain measured responses for some reused Trump/Eagles events and Oscars 2026; those were visible while satisfying the required repository review. This is a prospective freeze of this research selection, not a claim of blinded preregistration.
